messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Serving SLO breach detected
incident-bot: service=redwood-serving pool=dedicated-eu-west-2 metric=p99_latency_ms window=5m value=2100ms target=500ms queue_depth=avg: 420 (>200) autoscaler_delay=45s
oncall-amber: seeing it, joining now :eyes:
sre-liu: confirmed from tracing — tail tokens show long GC-like stalls in runtime on new instances during first requests (warmup path). p95 ~ 650ms, p99 ~ 2100ms. Streaming stalls spiking at the same time.
runtime-ops: looking at node logs, warmup is the KV-cache + jit path. New nodes spend ~30-50s compiling kernels for this model variant. autoscaler added 3 nodes at 23:07:12 but they only became ready at 23:08:00+
ml-eng-javier: model is a large quantized LLM with dynamic kernels, first request does heavy compilation. We have a coldpath cost.
product-anna: CS reporting multiple customers seeing timeouts on streaming endpoints. Any workaround we can patch to reduce impact quickly?
cs-sam: customer A (fintech) reported partial outages for 3 endpoints, grading severity P1, customer B degraded but still functional. They're asking for ETA.
oncall-amber: immediate mitigation plan: 1) pause new low-priority traffic to pool, 2) route critical traffic to hosted-fallback pool (smaller model), 3) manual scale with pre-warmed instances if possible. Can ops do those steps?
runtime-ops: can do 1 & 3. For 3 I can start prewarm instances using the hotstart script. However prewarming consumes reserved capacity and takes ~40s. Starting now.
runtime-ops: command run: ```
# start 4 prewarm nodes in eu-west-2
./infra/scale.sh --pool dedicated-eu-west-2 --count 4 --prewarm
```
sre-liu: also dropping non-streaming connections that exceed 60s to avoid head-of-line blocking. Will update throttling rules.
ml-eng-javier: as a medium-term mitigation we can serve a trimmed model variant that avoids heavy JIT kernels. I can bake a variant and push to canary in ~2h. For now suggest fallback routing.
product-anna: please draft a short customer note saying we see increased tail latency, routing to fallback models where appropriate, working on fixes. cs-sam can you handle outreach?
cs-sam: yes, sending msg to affected customers now. ETA for prewarm readiness?
runtime-ops: prewarm nodes show initializing. Logs: ```
[23:07:12] autoscaler: requested +3
[23:07:30] init: pulling image
[23:08:05] runtime: compiling kernels (estimated 35s)
[23:08:45] runtime: kv-cache populating
[23:08:55] node: ready
```
incident-bot: :white_check_mark: manual-prewarm initiated by runtime-ops :hammer:
oncall-amber: rolling throttle policy now: reduce concurrency for lower-tier API keys, keep enterprise/whitelisted customers at full throughput. Can we make that rule effective in 30s?
sre-liu: applying ACL now. Patch snippet: ```
# nginx-like proxy rules
if (api_key_tier == "free") {
  max_concurrency = 2
}
```
ml-eng-javier: quick check — streaming stalls are mostly on requests that hit the cold graph compile path. If we avoid first-request compile by issuing a lightweight probing request during prewarm that touches the main paths, warmup time drops to ~5s. We can add a probe script to prewarm flow.
runtime-ops: implementing probe now. Probe script: ```
curl -X POST https://local-runtime/health/probe -d '{"model":"x-large","input":"warmup"}'
```
product-anna: good. After prewarm, any idea when P99 will drop below target?
sre-liu: anticipating improvements: prewarm + probe -> p99 should drop to ~480-600ms within 2 min of readiness. Still monitoring for residual stalls.
cs-sam: messaging sent to customers: "We're routing traffic to backup pools and taking steps to prewarm capacity. Some streaming requests may get transient degraded quality as we switch models; working to restore normal latency."
oncall-amber: escalation: paging infra-lead if prewarm fails or p99 stays > 1500ms after 10m. Who's infra-lead? @sre-liu is covering but please ping infra-lead if not resolved.
runtime-ops: note—autoscaler logs show scale decisions delayed due to control-plane API throttling. Filing ticket to infra team. For now manual prewarm is fastest.
ml-eng-javier: will also push a tiny patch to runtime config to skip JIT for the first N requests (so those requests return faster albeit slightly slower per-token later). That should reduce stall severity. Deploy in ~20m to canary.
sre-liu: added temporary alert: if queue_depth > 300 for >2m, auto-run prewarm and throttle low-tier traffic automatically.
oncall-amber: any customer-facing downtime to mention? CS says no full outage yet, partial timeouts and slow streaming. Keep them updated.
product-anna: taking notes for postmortem: causes suspects = kernel JIT coldpath + autoscaler control-plane delay + no probe in prewarm flow. Mitigations = probe, fallback model routing, prewarm automation, throttling low-tier keys, faster autoscaler retries.
cs-sam: customers acknowledged the update, asking for timeline for full remediation. Told them 2 hours for canary and 24-48h for full roll.
runtime-ops: prewarm nodes ready at 23:09:05. Running probe, results show kernel compile hit and warmed caches. Preliminary metrics: p99 -> 520ms, queue_depth falling to 110.
incident-bot: :white_check_mark: SLOs improving — p99 5m now 520ms p95 420ms. Continue to monitor.
oncall-amber: leaving handoff to daytime oncall. If it degrades again, escalate to paging infra-lead. Good job all. :clap:
product-anna: will open a postmortem ticket and schedule root cause review with ML and infra teams.
ml-eng-javier: will prepare follow-up: bake a non-jit model variant and prewarm probe improvements.
sre-liu: adding runbook step for prewarm probes and a defensive guard in autoscaler to prefer prewarm over delayed scale in burst.
cs-sam: continuing outreach to affected customers, logging impact windows.
incident-bot: Incident resolved for now. Closing thread on stable metrics, reopen if regressions detected. :white_flag:"
